plotSections.title: Split clocks
bullets: The party is split. Walker is on the Reach; Ord, Gerk, and Sylan are at Carlkin's lighthouse, still on the same day. The faster-moving group is the controlling clock. Walker can end his side early; if their one-week return window runs out first, his remaining Reach time is montaged and he rejoins them.

He promised to be back within about one Midgar week of their time, not a week of his own. As this stretch opens, about five days and a morning have passed for them and about eleven days for him, so he is still inside that week.

plotSections.title: Carlkin on keystones, doors, and the lich
bullets: Play resumes at Carlkin's lighthouse with a second NPC also present. Sylan never made an agenda and expects to spitball. They have already told Carlkin that they hold keystones, that Gerk is a doorman who opened a door in the lighthouse onto the abyss, and that they are hunting a lich whose phylactery is a mundane item he kept on his person. They have already nearly brought an abyssal leviathan into the shop.

Sylan asks whether Carlkin has questions. Carlkin asks why they came, and Sylan starts to say they hoped his long knowledge of the area would help; the answer is cut off. Carlkin speaks for people who were once gatekeepers, not doormen: their job was to take a keystone and hide it. He finds it strange that keystones are being handed out again after so much effort spent collecting them. A lich pursuing the party and speaking to them telepathically alarms him, and he tells them to deal with that immediately.

Gerk's doors come from nothing and need no keystone. He can open and close one from either side, and only he can close it. Left open, it stays a gateway until the space-time continuum collapses. He is both Doorman and gatekeeper; Carlkin jokes that he could be called a gate doorman or a portcullis man. Only the Doorman can open that kind of portal. Keystone gates work only in certain situations, are one-way, and the keystone becomes part of the gate, so it cannot be carried through. Other travel exists: plane shift, dimension door, teleport, and teleportation circles. The Navi have their own methods, including a small rod that teleports directionally across Atlas.

Carlkin tells Gerk to practice somewhere empty, such as the woods or a large field, never underwater and not in the lighthouse. He will mend the floor himself, thanks them for trying, and is drinking. Sylan wants to practice at the castle, away from onlookers; Carlkin prefers the mountains, where no one can interfere. Gerk mentions dragons there, Sylan mentions a previous giant fight, and Carlkin has heard a rumor that the dragon is dead.

Gerk keeps trying to level the hole he made, tapping the floor by hand after being told to stop. He is sour because he asked for help, Carlkin did not listen, and the damage is treated as his fault. Carlkin compares him to a toddler in a sandbox and says the floor is nearly level.

plotSections.title: Leaving the lighthouse
bullets: Gerk had been opening doors to get the party in before he understood he should not, and he refuses to take further risks with them. Carlkin tells him that if the danger is that severe he should stay away from actual doors and immediately put down the thing that is dropping his arm. Gerk takes that as an order to discard the last memory of his mother.

Carlkin, drunk and still reeling from the eldritch horror in his living room, says Gerk's mother will not come through the portal, but everyone else will. Gerk says Carlkin called out him and his dead mother at least three times and that he might punch Carlkin one day. He breaks down in tears, nearly rages, and has to be dragged out, babbling. Sylan thinks he may need healing.

Sylan apologizes for the floor, the door, and whatever Gerk is about to do. Carlkin would rather they make an appointment than drop in. Gerk tries to climb out a window. Carlkin's warning was about Gerk's supernatural doors and his durability, not the ordinary lighthouse door. Sylan walks him out through that door and closes it behind them.

Sylan asks that when their comrade returns, Carlkin's people look at a helm. Carlkin agrees and will set the appointment by runner. They are farther than five hundred feet from the castle, so it is a walk rather than a sending. It is midday and they are outside.

plotSections.title: Walker returns to the Dragon Rider cave
bullets: Walker's Reach thread picks up from his discovery of an earth, wind, sea, and fire sigil, after contact with Vecna that the DM frames as opened communication, possibly a book club. He has been deciphering a drawn page: an obelisk, an island, a waterfall, and a mountain peak. Relative to the old tower of the dragon rider guild, those landmarks are shifted off their true positions.

He is in the ruins of the Dragon Rider guild keep, comparing the tower view with notes from the cave below. All he has is a strangely rotated image of the landmarks, and he believes there is more downstairs. He left because Vecna was in the cave, will not go back until Vecna is gone, and will not write in the book to ask. How he would know Vecna had left is unresolved at first.

He waits a couple of hours while Plymouth Gawater does scribe work and takes etchings, and he asks Glimmen whether Vecna is still down there. A notice arrives that a deity has left the realm, and Walker and Glimmen go back down. The smell has faded to a faint linger. The room is empty, the chair is pushed back, and the troop marker Vecna had been tapping is still on the table. The rest of the room is as they left it.

plotSections.title: The roost, etchings, and troop markers
bullets: The room holds an empty roost, cave etchings, a map table, and three extra stone chairs carved like the table. The etchings run in order around the walls as a panorama of a location above. They do not follow the cardinal directions; every sketch is rotated the same way clockwise. Walker thinks the shared offset is a clue, and the DM confirms he is onto something. There is no carved map, no compass in the floor, and no manifesto.

The table is a flat stone slab about four feet by four feet. Troop markers are scattered on the floor. They are black stone and ivory, or possibly a dark metal or bronze: knight-like cavalry, small etched dragons, pawns marked for rank or unit size, and flat poker-chip tokens in two matched sets. Walker sets the ordinary pieces on the table. A marker taken off this table in an earlier vision is missing; that vision is how the party connected the scene to the Raskina. He does not know what the scattered markers are for, and he distinguishes them from Vecna's special piece.
The piece Vecna was tapping, which Walker is still holding, is a high-ranking hunched eagle on a decorative base, not one of the chips.

plotSections.title: Ley lines and Grixto's moved convergence
bullets: Elrus has been shadowing Walker, as Walker assumed. He names the etched landmarks: an unnamed flat island of rolling green plains, about the size of the island they are on and sometimes written as the grassy atoll; Mount Elcastar; and Monkey Falls, marked by an old obsidian ley-line marker.

Walker knows neither the Weave nor ley lines. Elrus says the Weave is the magical network, briefly visible when energy is used, and ley lines are concentrations of it formed over ages. Some credit Atlas's rotation; others treat them as a magical latitude and longitude. They are not tunnels between planes. Standing on a line bolsters spells, an intersection is like stepping into a fire pit while already on fire, and teleportation and other magic cost less energy. A spell has to be cast within feet of a convergence. Markers can drift over millennia. Mages sought the lines out and fought over them, so many markers were moved or hidden. Convergences are rare; Elrus has seen only a few. He says Walker's training has to catch up or he will never beat Grixto.

The clockwise shift is the point: the carving shows where the old marker or intersection would be, and the rotated position is where the convergence is now. Grixto found this ley line, and the line had to have been moved. The landmark Viablis has stood since Elrus was a boy and is only rumored to be a ley line, so Elrus finds it concerning that Grixto carved it. Elrus means to visit the convergence soon if their other business comes to nothing. Walker calls it the clearest lead they have had. Elrus says they have only been in the cave a few hours and blames the time dilation.

plotSections.title: Lichdom, the eagle, and meditation
bullets: Walker asks whether a lich is made by a spell or by designating an object, using a glove as the example. Elrus says phylacteries are usually gems and that the working is an ancient ritual whose exact method he does not know. The Al Kurin was to aid Grixto's lichdom. The Al Kurin, a ley-line convergence, and the Raskina together are a deadly combination. Ley lines would help a lich by strengthening magic, not by carrying anyone between planes.

Elrus dismisses the troop markers as unnecessary for the immediate question. He reads the eagle as a legion standard and notes that Grixto was a hobgoblin, whose legions would carry an eagle. Without a map he cannot say what the figurines are for. Walker still feels he is missing something. He pockets the eagle.

Elrus has him set aside what he is holding and sit in the cave to work through the rituals Grixto laid out: where he must go, what he needs to get there, and the puzzle in front of him. Elrus sits cross-legged in the middle of the room and coaches nose-and-diaphragm breathing, a wave-like breath, and a sense of the floor. Walker follows. The scene leaves them meditating.

plotSections.title: Sixth day in New Navel
bullets: Ord, Gerk, and Sylan are outside Carlkin's lighthouse at midday on their sixth day, with a day and a half left before a deadline the DM does not finish naming. New Navel is busy with ordinary traffic.

Sylan wants to rest, wait to hear from Walker, and then train Gerk's doorway on short distances. Gerk worries something will go wrong; Sylan says they solved it last time, and Gerk notes that was with violence. Gerk suggests opening onto Carlkin's living room. Sylan puts that off until tomorrow because Carlkin told them not to use doors in his house. Gerk's distinction is that he would not be inside the house when he opened one.

They go to the party's pub rather than straight back to the stronghold. Ciri is already in the corner, crouched as if hidden, too drunk to keep stealthing, with a pile of mugs. The night is a drinking montage. The basement is finished and can hold cold storage. Owners are not charged. Locals recognize the party; newer faces are travelers and traders from Dullhurst and beyond, in town for trade at New Navel / Rita. Flavian is the name given for the manager. A middle-aged half-elf minstrel plays a classical lute while moving through the room instead of staying on a stage. They wake the next morning in the stronghold to the building shaking and the smell of fresh buns.

plotSections.title: Morning at Langdale and where to practice
bullets: Morning at Langdale Stronghold: the sun is up, the building is shaking, and fresh buns are baking. The established ratio is seven of Walker's days to one of the party's. About forty-two of his days have passed without a check-in. That is still inside the agreed Midgar week of their time, so he is not overdue and they are not yet worried. He is expected to arrive on Glimmen, and Mahali is to have food ready for the dragon.

Sylan has already been up for four hours. After breakfast he starts Gerk's doorway training. Gerk questions why Sylan is the one to train him, looks to Ord mid-bite of a bun, then accepts and asks whether Ord is coming. Ord comes to watch. Ciri spent the night in a room at the tavern, rejoins them still in the same clothes with her boots over one shoulder, and is face-down in the buns before she leaves with them.

They will not practice in the living room, because Gerk might open a portal to hell there. The lake has no island, they are not going to the bees, and they rule out old buildings and civilization as the target. They choose the southern forest clearing and stream from the earlier hobgoblin search. The DM ties previously found runes, heard as Paulette runes, to a red-flag marker a decent way into the woods. The party does not go to the runes; they only want to enter the forest out of view of the stronghold. Gerk has no preference between dirt and stone.
Sylan tells the guards that if Walker returns, the group went south into the forest and he may contact them. By mid-morning Sylan, Gerk, Ord, and Ciri are on the outskirts, ready to practice.

plotSections.title: Doorway tests: place, person, and a battlefield
bullets: They restate Gerk's rules: picture something very specific, do not think of nothing, never open underwater, always close the door, and do not open it while moving.

Gerk targets the field in front of the tavern, about twenty feet from the door, still in Langdale, and says so aloud. Sylan calls on the Raven Queen and grants Guidance. Gerk rolls a 16. The door opens about a quarter mile southwest of the intended spot, near the road from the tavern to New Navel. The tavern is visible in the distance, and from that angle most of the stronghold can be seen.

Sylan hops through and holds the door. Three human traders with a mule-drawn cart, about a football field away and headed the other way, are startled when he appears out of nothing. The portal faces away from them; they keep walking and only glance back. From the destination the opening is a stationary, featureless, door-shaped hole, like a green screen projecting the people on the other side, with sight and sound passing through. Sylan can see and hear Gerk, Ord, and Ciri in the forest. He calls it close enough and treats portal magic here as unsurprising.

He proposes targeting a person instead of a place. Gerk closes the door and focuses on Sylan, whom he knows is in this realm and whose general location he knows: about ten feet behind him, near his best friend at a respectful distance, and he does not want to head back without him. A natural 20 opens the door exactly there, with no flash and no frame; the only sign is forest birdsong from the place they left. Sylan concludes the doorway can work on a person as well as a place. Knowing the general location helped, and he suggests fondness may also matter; Gerk allows that it might. Sylan waits out the traders, then hops back.

They test a person whose exact spot Gerk does not know. Ciri hides in the woods: 7 on the die and 23 total, so the party still has a rough sense she is in the forest. Gerk covers his eyes and aims for a ten-foot circle around her, close but not too close, while admitting he knows she is in the forest. Sylan casts Guidance. The roll is 1 on the guidance die and 3 on the d20, total 4.

The door opens onto a maelstrom of explosions, flashes, and noise. In a trench embankment, an orc with a metal weapon crouches beside a human. Both wear mixed medieval and French Renaissance clothing and carry metal tube-sticks. One points a tube and shouts in an unknown language; the other fumbles a small clay pot from his belt. Gerk slams the door. The forest returns: birds, cool air, a brimstone-sulfur whiff, and a black smudge on the grass. Nothing else of that place remains, and he did not find Ciri. Sylan's working theory is that a person alone is not enough; the location has to be known, at least so far. Ciri throws her voice, then stays hidden in a tree and watches.

plotSections.title: A remembered door to Bouncing Betty
bullets: Sylan frames the next step as learning what activates the ability: emotion, rage, or a happy memory. Gerk calls making him angry a bad idea. The clean opening on Sylan is tied to having just seen him and knowing where he was, not only to fondness. Sylan proposes describing places they have been, including smell. Gerk says he is weak at that but will try. Sylan does not want to open a door home yet because the mission is unfinished, and he names Halo Heart as a good place to picture, but not to open here.

They try Volga as a memory exercise: the frozen gatehouse they climbed, tall, cold, and a little spooky, and the spear-in-the-head moment. Gerk only half remembers it. He chooses a tavern he has visited often and associates with friends, which he calls Twin Peaks and the group also calls Bouncing Betty. They cannot agree on the name, whether it has two floors or a third, or whether a stage they remember belongs to a different place. He aims for the upstairs hall outside the rooms, not the front door, which would drop them into a busy street. Sylan says the rooms have been moved.

Gerk pictures leaving an inn bedroom into that hall. Sylan casts Guidance. The check is 19, 16 plus 3. The DM had expected a miss and was not sure the tavern had a second floor. In game it has been a long time. Their last stop was before the one-to-two-month boat trip toward Lake Nyx: they picked up Plymouth for the Yowan and hid the last keystone until they arrived, a stop also tied to a dragon.

The door does open on Bouncing Betty, but confusion shifts it onto a stronger memory. Gerk comes out on the second story of the rebuilt barn, about twenty feet from the hallway he wanted, looking down on stables and a wagon in the center. He has slept in that barn. An old sideline there had a wayward bard and a drunk wizard levitate and kill a mule or donkey, leave the body in the barn, and earn the party some gold. He shuts the door before anyone can fall. It clicks and disappears. Sylan calls it a strong result for somewhere so far away, and a sign that places Gerk likes are easier to hit.

plotSections.title: The rage door and what closing cuts
bullets: Sylan thinks Gerk may simply improve with use, or that something in him still has to be unlocked. He recalls Carlkin saying they would not be able to open doors, and Plymouth Gawater saying that with time and practice they could use the keystones. Sylan does not intend to practice that yet; he says he has plenty of time and mentions his realm. Gerk refuses to let a key anywhere near him and says he will not fall for that trick again. The DM asks, "Again?"

Asked to try strength instead of a purely mental focus, Gerk agrees to open the door as hard as he can. Sylan sets a lantern about twenty feet away and steps back. Gerk turns his back, pictures that lantern, rages, and rips the doorway open under Guidance. He rolls a 17. The DM notes recent door results of 19, 16, a non-20, and a 4. An enormous door tears open, about eighteen feet tall and seven feet wide, into the same forest roughly a quarter mile south, marked by a disturbance of birds. It does not land on the lantern. Where it cuts through canopy, those branches sit in a semi-translucent limbo. Gerk can feel the door he opened and, separately, the presence of its far end.

Sylan suspects a harder opening makes a bigger door, and that this one might fit Glimmen. Gerk is unsure but hopes that is how it works. Sylan does not trust the portal enough to step through first. He and Ciri walk the quarter mile south. The far side reaches into the canopy, intersecting branches are translucent, and the forest floor is undisturbed: no crater and nothing catastrophic. Sylan still does not know what caused the racket. They return through the portal, Ciri passing as a shadow, and come out beside Gerk. Sylan suggests Gerk may need to know a place fondly, or remember it fondly, to place the exit accurately. Gerk does not know whether he can open a door beside himself or what his exact range is.

Next they try a normal, non-rage opening at a point Gerk can see, about twenty-five feet away across a crossing and past the lantern. Guidance is on the attempt. He rolls a 9. The door opens short of the chosen spot, over the lantern, and is again about eighteen feet tall. The first door is still open. Wind rushes between them, a vortex forms, and the lantern is pulled through the new door into the far one. Gerk shuts both and the wind dies. To the south, branches crash down.

Where limbs had passed through the doorway, they are cleanly severed, with no burn and no loose debris, as if sliced by a blade. The fallen branches lie in a pile. The lantern is dinged and disheveled, not shattered. They treat the shear as extremely dangerous: useful against something huge, or maybe a rope bridge, and unsafe in a crowd or when opening onto a person. Gerk recalls Carlkin telling them to practice in the middle of a field. They were lucky the earlier kitchen opening did not cut Mahali, which the DM calls a critical success, and they connect the effect to the boat that was ripped out of reality. A doorway opened three times a day seems to surface recent destinations as favorites. Recent places may be easier. Gerk does not want another try yet; Sylan says they have time.

plotSections.title: The tomato-field door
bullets: Sylan wants a doorway toward his sister so they can get in and out quickly. Gerk refuses, citing the attempt on Ciri when he did not know where she was. Sylan suggests Dana's boost and songs, or another spell, if they can learn which ability the door uses. Gerk says it just happens. They already know a forceful opening makes a bigger door.

Gerk instead tries a gentle, low, dog-sized door about a hundred feet in front of a house, aimed clear of the tomato field. Sylan gives Guidance. Gerk rolls an 18. The opening is about six to eight inches by twelve inches, but it lands in the tomato field about a foot off the ground, where it could cut a stem. It is fall, and this garden is currently always in tomato.

Gerk pulls a large tomato plant through. On a perception of 10, something on the far side growls, snaps, and tugs the plant. Red and green tomatoes scatter. He cuts the stalk with a dagger while Sylan tells him to keep a hand on the door. The rest of the plant snaps back, and the creature scrabbles, growls, and rams the closed door.

While his hand is on the shut door, impacts feel like an ordinary door and they cannot see the far side. The door stays at whatever opening his hand leaves it at. A hard enough hit can shove him and swing it open; if his hand comes off, it remains at that position until he lets go entirely. He releases it during a lull. The outline dissipates, the growling stops, and the space returns to normal. He will not reopen it. Sylan reads that as proof Gerk can keep working a door while he is operating it, including after closing it. He guesses the growling thing is the householder's pet and calls keeping it out the work of door guardians, a name they have not settled.

They stop for the day. Gerk hands out tomatoes as snacks. They decline a portal back to the stronghold and ride their mounts, arriving around midday. The morning's training showed that Gerk can open these portals seemingly at will, with caveats.

plotSections.title: The landmark table and primal stones
bullets: Walker has been meditating the whole time and still does not understand the puzzle Grixto set. Elrus takes the hunched eagle from his pocket and sets it with cavalry and infantry tokens on a square table he has makeshift assembled, asking for the cavalry markers, not the rams. The eagle has nothing to do with a mountain or a waterfall. Walker guesses it is a tuning fork before the explanation continues.

Placing the hunched eagle makes the table flash. Four cardinal tokens become landmark representations, troop markings appear as a small semi-animated illusion, and a partial battlefield map fills in around them. Walker remembers Vecna tapping this same kind of piece during their conversation, and Grixto taking a different hunched eagle from a table and leaving with the plan sorted. The table is an illusion item that can project or reenact a battle if the right tokens are placed. The flat tokens they have are already at their usable limit; more known landmarks or other pieces would extend the map. How the tokens are made is unknown. Elrus reads this as how Grixto worked as a military planner and says they are in over their heads. Walker thinks Grixto may have had a similar table in a command center where they first met him; he cannot settle the place name, and it is not confirmed.

On the map the obelisk sits fifteen degrees off where it should, which Elrus takes to mean a conveyance is there. Both of them think it is worth checking. Near a conveyance, Walker's wards and shields would be amplified, then return to normal a short time after he leaves. Channeling to force a stronger lasting effect is possible but untrained and could erase him. Elrus says that with more he could probably channel, and that they should meditate further.

Walker's gems already glow with energy he has been putting into them at the cost of exhaustion. Elrus once carried similar gems and gave them to other prospective riders. He offers primal stones: raw magic condensed into a stone. The maker would no longer be the only one directing it. A craftsperson could shape it into an item or call the energy, or it could be broken in desperation for a torrent of power. Condensing it could cost Walker part of himself. He wants to learn more. Elrus says he must pick a primal magic and asks whether he is attuned to any of the sources.

chronologicalEvents: The DM sets the split-party clock: the faster group controls the timeline, and Walker's leftover scenes will be montaged when the party's one-week timer ends unless he ends early. Walker is on the Reach on a slower arrangement relative to the lighthouse group. Five days and a morning have passed for the party since they left him; he has lived eleven days, just over two of their days. He spoke with Vecna and may have joined a book club, and he has been deciphering a page of radially shifted landmarks—an obelisk, an island, a waterfall, and a mountain—as seen from the dragon rider guild's old tower, following an earth, wind, sea, and fire sigil. The table then returns to Ord, Gerk, and Sylan with Carlkin.

Play resumes the same day in Carlkin's lighthouse. Gerk keeps repairing the hole in the floor despite being told to stop, and is upset that Carlkin ignored his ask for help. Sylan asks whether Carlkin has questions. Carlkin asks why they came, and Sylan says they hoped his long knowledge and presence would cover what they are facing, including the lich.

Carlkin, a former gatekeeper rather than a doorman, explains that gatekeepers hid keystones and were not doormen. He warns that redistributing keystones is strange and that a lich speaking to them telepathically should be dealt with immediately. He tells Gerk to practice doors only in the woods or a large field, never underwater and not in the lighthouse, and to always shut a door he opens or it remains a gateway until space-time collapses. He recalls that they already nearly brought an abyssal leviathan into his shop, says he will mend the floor later, and drinks. He confirms Gerk can open and close his door from either side without a keystone, while keystone gates are situational, one-way, and bind the keystone into the gate. He distinguishes that portal from plane shift, dimension door, teleport, teleportation circles, and a Navi rod that teleports directionally across Atlas.

They tentatively plan door practice at the castle or in the mountains. Sylan prefers the castle; Carlkin prefers the mountains, where the party mentions dragons and giants and where Carlkin has heard the dragon is dead. Carlkin says the castle is farther than five hundred feet away.

Gerk admits he opened the doors to enter before he knew he should not, and refuses to risk opening more. Carlkin tells him to stay away from real doors and to put down the door that is dropping his arm. Gerk tries to leave by the window because he took the warning not to use doors literally, and is told the ban was on his doorway ability rather than physical doors. He breaks down over losing the last memory of his mother, the keepsake on his arm, rages when it is dismissed, and has to be dragged from the room. Carlkin says Gerk's mother will not come to the portal, though everyone else will. Sylan moves Gerk back down through the floor with only the door and suggests he may need healing.

They agree to leave and to make an appointment next time. Sylan asks Carlkin to examine a helm once a comrade returns, via a runner. Sylan thanks him, closes the doors, and the group is outside at midday.

Walker, at the ruined Dragon Rider guild keep, compares a rotated landmark image and his notes with the cave drawings below. He refuses to return while Vecna is down there or to contact him through the book, and waits a couple of hours. Plymouth remains at the site doing scribe work and etchings.

A notification pings that a deity has left the realm. Walker and Glimmen go back down. The cave is empty, the smell only faint, the chair pushed back, and Vecna's tapped troop marker is still on the table. The DM confirms that a troop marker removed in the earlier vision would not still be in the room, and that the clockwise tilt of the cave sketches is a real tell.

The wall etchings run in order around the cave and do not line up with the cardinal directions. Walker treats that offset as a clue, and it is confirmed he is onto something. There is no carved map, no floor compass, and no manifesto. The table is a flat stone slab about four feet square. The room holds an empty roost, scattered troop markers, etchings of a place above, the table, and three extra stone chairs.

Walker sorts the markers into cavalry knights, dragons, ranked pawns, and two sets of poker-chip tokens. Vecna's piece, which Walker is still holding, is a high-ranking hunched eagle with a decorative base. The marker removed in the earlier vision is absent. The group distinguishes these markers from Al Kurin and from the Raskina, identified in the vision as the sister-skin book.

Elrus, shadowing Walker, names the etchings: the grassy atoll, Mount Elcastar, and Monkey Falls with an old obsidian ley-line marker. He explains the Weave and ley lines as a crisscrossing magical boundary, finds that Walker knows neither, and says that gap has to close if Walker is going to beat Grixto. He describes drifting markers, and how a convergence bolsters spells and cheapens teleportation without being a road between planes. Viablis is an old landmark only rumored to be a ley line.

Elrus reads the four shifted carvings as Grixto marking a ley line that moved, where a spell must be cast within feet of the convergence, and links that site to Al Kurin and the Raskina for lichdom. Walker asks how lichdom works. Elrus calls it an ancient ritual, usually using gems, and treats the Al Kurin, the convergence, and the Raskina as the dangerous combination. They agree the convergence is worth visiting if their other business stalls. Elrus attributes the sense that hours feel like weeks to time dilation, calls the eagle a legion standard tied to hobgoblin Grixto, cannot explain the figurines without a map, and has Walker pocket the eagle and meditate with him in the cave to unwind the rituals Grixto put forward. Walker sits, breathing through the nose and diaphragm, thinking about where he must go.

The view shifts to the rest of the party outside Carlkin's lighthouse at midday on day six, with a day and a half remaining. Sylan proposes rest and, tomorrow, short-range practice of Gerk's doorway. Gerk floats a short jump to Carlkin's living room despite the ban on doors in the house; Sylan delays that until tomorrow.

Ord, Sylan, and Gerk go to the pub and find Ciri already drunk in the corner, stealth blown, surrounded by mugs. The tavern night passes with staff including a woman the DM calls Flavian, a finished cold-storage basement, locals and traders, and a wandering half-elf lutenist. The party sleeps it off.

They wake at Langdale Stronghold to shaking stone and fresh buns. The check-in is clarified as one Midgar week of party time, with seven of Walker's days equaling one party day. Roughly forty-two Walker-days have passed and he has not checked in, which does not mean he is late.

After breakfast in the great hall, Sylan takes Gerk's training. Gerk accepts, and Ord and Ciri join. They rule out the stronghold living room and confirm there is no island in the lake. They consider the southern stream clearing from the hobgoblin search, skip the bees and old ruins, and settle on riding into the forest out of sight of the stronghold.

Sylan tells the guards to inform Walker, expected to arrive on Glimmen, that the group went south into the forest and can be contacted, and asks Mahali to prepare food for the dragon. Ciri, who stayed in a tavern room, meets them on the stronghold path and joins. Asked about previously found runes marked by the red flag, they instead stop mid-morning on the forest outskirts, out of view, to practice.

They review the doorway rules. Gerk targets a point about twenty feet from the tavern door while Sylan grants Guidance. On a 16, the door opens roughly a quarter mile southwest, with the tavern and most of the stronghold visible. Sylan steps through onto the tavern-to-New Navel road and startles three human traders with a mule cart about a football field away. The portal carries sound and a view of the forest side, but is otherwise an invisible, featureless door. Gerk closes it.

Gerk targets Sylan about ten feet behind him. On a natural 20 the door opens exactly there, silently, noticeable only by forest birdsong from the area they left. Guards startle, then walk on, glancing back. Sylan hops back through. They note that a person can be targeted, that knowing the general location helped, and that thought, memory, or fondness might matter. Sylan asks which of those Gerk uses.

Ciri hides in the forest with a stealth roll of 7 against a 23, throws her voice, then stays in a tree and watches. Gerk covers his eyes and, guided by Sylan, tries to open a door near her without knowing the exact spot. The total is 4. The door opens onto an explosion-filled trench where an orc and a human in mixed medieval and Renaissance dress level metal tubes and reach for a clay pot. Gerk shuts it. A sulfur smell and a black smudge remain on the grass. He did not find Ciri, and Sylan suggests a known location may be required, not only a person.

Sylan trains Gerk on emotion or rage versus a detailed memory of a place. Gerk rejects being made angry. They recall that the door to Sylan worked because Gerk had just seen him. Sylan withholds a door home until the mission is done, names Halo Heart as a picture to hold, and walks Gerk through the frozen gatehouse at Volga, which they climbed: cold, tall, and mildly spooky. Gerk does not remember it clearly. He instead chooses Twin Peaks, a place he knows well with fond memories of friends, and aims for the upstairs hallway of its tavern, outside the inn rooms and away from the street-facing front door. They argue the tavern's name and layout, and whether Bouncing Betty or another tavern was the one with the stage. They agree to try a short stop there after the current training; they had said they would be in the forest, and Nawaka can message them.

Gerk aims a doorway from a Bouncing Betty bedroom to that upstairs hallway. The group places their last visit long before the boat trip to Nyx, around collecting Plymouth and only then revealing the last keystone. With Sylan's Guidance the check totals 19. Confusion shifts the opening about twenty feet onto the loft of Bouncing Betty's rebuilt barn, above the stables and a central wagon, toward the more familiar memory of nights Gerk slept there and of a bard, a drunk wizard, and a levitated dead donkey or mule that earned the party some gold. Gerk closes the door; it clicks and vanishes. Sylan praises the distance and accuracy for a liked place, then weighs more practice against unlocking something in Gerk. He contrasts Carlkin's claim that they could not open doors with Plymouth Gawater's claim that practice and time would let them use the keystones. Gerk rejects having a key put near him, citing a trick he will not fall for again.

Sylan coaches Gerk to put his hammer-swinging strength into the doorway and places a lantern about twenty feet away as a focus. Gerk faces away, pictures the lantern, rages, and opens the door as hard as he can with Guidance, rolling a 17. An eighteen-foot-tall, seven-foot-wide door tears open onto the same forest about a quarter mile south. Birds disturb the far end, branches intersecting the doorway turn semi-translucent, and Gerk feels both this door and the far door.

Sylan and a hidden Ciri walk south through the woods instead of stepping through. They find the far door reaching into the canopy, translucent where it cuts branches, with no crater or other destruction, then return through the portal. Sylan suggests fond memory may be required for accurate placement. Gerk is unsure of his range.

Gerk attempts a normal line-of-sight doorway about twenty-five feet away, past the lantern, with Guidance, and rolls a 9. The door opens short, over the lantern. Because the eighteen-foot doorway is still open, wind vortices between the two doors suck the lantern from one into the other. Gerk closes both. The wind stops, and branches crash to the south. Sylan finds the intersecting limbs cleanly cut and unburned, recovers the dinged lantern, and warns that closing a door can slice whatever it intersects. They agree the shear is a hazard in crowds and when opening onto people, and stop further tests of that kind for now.

They decide not to doorway to Sylan's sister. They talk through Dana boosting the attempt and the fact that forcing the door makes it bigger; Gerk still does not know what ability he is using. With Guidance, he gently opens a doggy door a few inches across toward the field in front of a tomato-grower's house and rolls an 18. It lands in the tomato plants. He hauls a plant through. Something on the other side growls, fights him for it, and scrabbles against the door. He cuts the stalk, which snaps back, and slams the door while keeping a hand on the handle so Sylan can test whether a closed door still exists.

While Gerk holds it, the closed door stays, takes a ram from the far side like an ordinary door, and holds at the angle where his hand leaves it; a hard shove while he is still holding it would swing it open. He lets go in a lull. The outline vanishes, the creature's noise stops, and he refuses to reopen it. They snack on tomatoes, skip portaling home, and ride back, arriving around midday after a morning of practice.

The scene returns to Walker, still meditating with Elrus on Grixto's puzzle. Elrus takes the hunched-eagle marker and the cavalry and infantry tokens and lays them on the square table, with the eagle disconnected from the mountain and the waterfall, and asks for the cavalry markers. Placing the hunched eagle flashes the table into a partial illusion map of four cardinal landmark tokens and smaller troop markers. Memory shows Vecna toggling such a piece, and Grixto taking a different hunched eagle from a table once the plan was set.

The projected obelisk is fifteen degrees off true, which Elrus reads as a conveyance at that spot. Wards would be stronger only while near the conveyance. He warns Walker off untrained channeling and describes primal stones as stored raw magic Walker could try to condense, at the risk of losing part of himself. Elrus asks which primal source Walker is attuned to, and Walker has not yet answered.

Walker.existing: Half-elf dragon rider and fighter, Gatekeeper of The Reach, bonded to Glimmen.
notes: Spoke with Vecna, which the DM treats as Walker having started communicating with him, and he may now be in a book club with Vecna. He does not want to speak to Vecna again immediately.

On the Reach alone while Ord, Gerk, and Sylan are with Carlkin. About five days and a morning of party time have passed since they left him; he has lived about eleven days, counted as a little over two days for them. His time runs about seven days to each party day. By the practice morning about forty-two of his days have passed. He promised to check in after one Midgar week of their time, so they are not yet due to hear from him.
The party's clock controls the split. When their one-week window ends, his remaining time is montaged and he rejoins, unless he stops early.

He is in the Dragon Rider guild keep ruins, matching cave drawings to the surface. His sketch of an obelisk, an island, a waterfall, and a mountain is rotated from the view at the old guild tower, and he thinks the record is incomplete. His separate thread last ended on an earth, wind, sea, and fire sigil. He found no map, compass, or written plan.
He left the cave because Vecna was there and will not write in the book to ask if Vecna is still below. A deity-left-the-realm notice brings him and Glimmen back to an empty room.
He had not been taught the Weave or ley lines. He reads the shared offset of the etchings as a clue and wants to reach the ley-line landmark.

He set the troop markers on the table, pocketed the hunched eagle Vecna had been tapping, and later hands it over. He asks what an eagle has to do with a mountain or a waterfall, is told nothing, and guesses it is a tuning fork as the scene cuts away.

He agrees the convergence is the best lead and meditates in the cave with Elrus on Grixto's puzzle. He still does not understand what he was told to look for until Elrus uses the table. The cutaway leaves him in that meditation.

He has been spending energy and taking exhaustion to charge gems that now glow, and he hopes to learn primal stones. Near a conveyance his wards and shields would be amplified, then fade after he leaves. Untrained channeling could channel him out of existence.
Expected back at the stronghold on Glimmen rather than by carriage, and invited to contact the others once told they went south into the forest. The stronghold is to be ready to feed the dragon.
personality: His immediate priority is not speaking to Vecna again.
quotesThemes: He said he would talk to the party in a week, meaning one Midgar week of their time.
openQuestions: Is Walker attuned to any primal source?

Vecna.existing: Elder god of liches who watches from the periphery and pursues hidden knowledge.
notes: He talked with Walker in the cave under the Dragon Rider guild ruins, in a conversation tied to the landmark diagram. The DM suggests Walker may now be in a book club with him. Walker refuses to write in the book to ask whether he is still below.

He has left the realm. A deity-left notification fires while Walker waits above, and the room is empty when Walker returns. His strong smell has faded to a faint linger. No manifesto or written plan was left.

He left his chair pushed back. In the vision and in Walker's memory he sat tapping a high-ranking hunched-eagle troop marker on and off. That piece stayed on the table; Walker later pocketed it. He is associated with special rocks, distinct from the ordinary markers scattered in the room.

Tilted landmarks.existing: Cardinal cave carvings set a few degrees off true bearing.
notes: Four etchings in the Dragon Rider cave, panoramic and in sequence around the walls: an obelisk, an island, a waterfall, and a mountain. They are not a map, not a compass rose, and not carved into the table.

Judged from the old dragon rider guild tower, they are radially off their true bearings. Walker has only a rotated sketch from the cave drawings and at first cannot read the offset. All four are rotated the same way, clockwise.

They correspond to the grassy atoll, Mount Elcastar, and Monkey Falls. Elrus reads the shared rotation as the message: it moves the old ley-line intersection to the convergence Grixto found. On the token map the obelisk is fifteen degrees off, which Elrus reads as a conveyance at that location.

Dragon Rider Training Grounds.existing: Dragon rider guild training grounds near the Lost Isles.
notes: Walker is in the ruins of the guild keep. The old tower is the standing point for the radially shifted landmark diagram.
Below is the cave room where Vecna had been sitting: wall etchings and a flat stone table about four feet by four feet. Walker will not go back down until he believes Vecna is gone.
Plymouth is on site taking etchings and doing scribe work.

The Reach.existing: Largest Arch realm of Atlas; Walker is its Gatekeeper.
notes: Walker is there alone relative to the lighthouse scene. His local time runs longer than the party's: about eleven of his days against a little over two of theirs, with the departure also put at five days and a morning.

Carlkin.existing: Turtle-like person; lighthouse, home, and bookshop in New Navel.
notes: Ord, Gerk, and Sylan are still with him in the lighthouse on the day they already briefed him. A second person is present; the DM invites questions to either, and this stretch does not separate that voice from his.

He and the people he speaks for were once gatekeepers. Their work was protection: receive a keystone and hide it. They were not doormen. He finds it strange that keystones are being handed out again after they were collected.
A lich speaking to the party telepathically unsettles him. He tells them to deal with the lich immediately. He has heard a rumor that the dragon in the mountains is dead.

He tells Gerk to stop fixing the hole. Gerk keeps going. Carlkin will mend the floor later and thanks them for trying. He wants practice in the woods or a large field, never underwater and not in the lighthouse or his house, and says only Gerk can shut those doors.

He says an unshut door stays a gateway until the space-time continuum collapses. He tells Gerk to put down the door that is dropping Gerk's arm, and that Gerk's mother will not come through the portal though everyone else will. He invokes Gerk and Gerk's dead mother at least three times.

He drinks through the talk and is quite drunk by the end, still reeling from an eldritch horror brought into his living room. He would rather they book an appointment than arrive unannounced, and agrees to send a runner and schedule a look at a helm when their comrade returns.
His location is much farther than five hundred feet from the castle.
personality: Dry, blunt, and pedantic, and increasingly drunk. Fussy about his floor and about doors left open. He treats Gerk's repair like a toddler in a sandbox while still thanking him, then prods Gerk about his dead mother and brushes it off.
quotesThemes: Asks whether they came for no real reason or what they actually want from him.
If a door is never shut, it stays a gateway until the space-time continuum collapses, and that is only scary if Gerk does not close it.
Never practice opening doors underwater.
Keystone gates are one-way, and the keystone becomes part of the gate.
Gerk's mother will not come through the portal; everyone else will.
Next time, make an appointment.
openQuestions: Why the party came to Carlkin. Sylan only begins to say that Carlkin is knowledgeable and has been around a long time.

Gerk.existing: Half-orc barbarian, Doorman, Child of the Tree, Midgar keystone keeper.
notes: Still trying to repair the lighthouse hole after Carlkin told him to stop, tapping the floor level by hand. He had asked for help in his own way, Carlkin did not listen, and Gerk takes the blame as his fault.

He is both Doorman and gatekeeper. His doors come from nothing and need no keystone. He can open and close one from either side, and only he can shut it. Carlkin floats joke titles: gate doorman, door-gate man, and portcullis man.

After the warning he refuses even ordinary doors and climbs out a window. Carlkin clarifies that he meant the doorway ability. Gerk had already opened doors to get the party inside and will not take that risk again.

The thing on his arm is, to him, the last memory of his mother. Carlkin telling him to put that door down, and saying his mother will not come through the portal, pushes him to rage. He cries, babbles, and has to be dragged out. He says he may punch Carlkin one day.

He goes to the pub with Sylan and Ord. After breakfast he accepts Sylan as trainer and asks Ord to come. He will not practice in the living room after previously opening a portal toward hell, prefers somewhere remote, and does not care whether the ground is dirt or stone. There is no island in the stronghold lake. He goes south into the forest with Sylan, Ord, and Ciri.

He will not trigger the ability by being made angry, though he later rages and forces one opening. He says he is poor at vivid place descriptions but willing to practice. He describes the accurate door to Sylan as focusing on a respectful distance from his best friend, helped by having just seen him and knowing his general location.

He remembers Twin Peaks, including friends, better than Volga, and aims for the upstairs hallway of the tavern rather than the busy street. Confusion shifts that opening to the barn loft, a place he has slept, including the memory of the levitated donkey or mule. He shuts it before anyone falls through.
He refuses to have a key put on or near him and says he will not fall for that trick again. He will not try a doorway to Sylan's sister after the failed reach toward Ciri.

He can feel a door he has opened and the presence of its far end. He does not know what magic the door uses or how close he can place one. He shuts the battlefield door at once, cuts the tomato plant free, holds the shut door while something rams it, then lets go rather than reopen it onto the growling thing. He rides home instead of portaling to the stronghold.
personality: Stubborn about fixing what he broke, and sore when someone ignores the way he asks for help. Literal enough to leave by the window rather than use a forbidden door.
Grief over his mother turns quickly to rage. He treats Sylan as his best friend and frames a good door as staying near him without crowding him.
Wary of anyone bringing a key close to him. Willing to test the doorway by force, then quick to stop when the result is frightening, cutting, or hostile on the far side.
quotesThemes: Killing space and time by leaving a door open sounds scary.
The thing on his arm is the last memory of his mother.
He targets people by focusing on being close, but not too close, to a friend.
Making him mad to trigger the door sounds like a bad idea.
I don't think I found Ciri.
Safer to open into a hallway than the middle of a busy street.
You're not putting a key anywhere near me. I am not falling for that trick again.
Places he likes and remembers fondly are easier to open onto, even when the exact room is wrong.
openQuestions: What earlier trick involved putting a key near Gerk?

notes: He has no agenda for Carlkin and interviews him on door rules, starting to say they came because Carlkin is knowledgeable and has been around a long time. He presses whether Gerk can close a door from the far side, whether only the Doorman can open that portal, and whether Gerk needs the keys.

He apologizes for the floor, gets Gerk back down through the floor using only the door, thinks Gerk may need healing, closes the doors, and walks him out. Gerk does not use that door. He books a return appointment, including a look at the helm once a comrade is back.

He recalls Carlkin saying the party would not be able to open doors, set against Plymouth's advice that practice would let them use the keystones. He does not plan to practice his own keystone or realm yet and says he has plenty of time. He also remembers hiding the last keystone from Plymouth until they reached the Yowan.

On day six outside the lighthouse he calls for rest, word from Walker, and then short-range doorway practice. He defers Carlkin's living room because Carlkin said not to use doors in the house. He goes to the pub. Next morning he has already been up four hours. Gerk accepts him as trainer.

He chooses the southern forest clearing by the stream over the living room, the lake, the bees, and the red-flag runes. He tells the guards that if Walker returns, the group went south into the forest and Walker may contact them, and he expects Walker by dragon. He supports having Mahali prepare food for Glimmen.

He calls on the Raven Queen for Guidance, steps through Gerk's doors, and checks a far end on foot before using it, including walking a quarter mile south with Ciri. He proposes tests on a place, then a person, then a person whose exact position is unknown.

After the misses, his working theory is that the door needs a known location, not only a named person, and that fondness, a recent visit, or a stronger memory may place it more accurately. He coaches through emotion, happy memory, and sensory detail, including the frozen gatehouse at Volga, then switches to Twin Peaks when Volga is too faint. He offers Halo Heart as a picture and does not want a door home until the mission is finished.

He believes Gerk will improve with use, or that something in him still needs to be unlocked. He suggests rage and physical strength as a trial, then judges the cutting effect wildly dangerous and says not to use it in a crowd or when opening onto a person.

He wants a later doorway to his sister so they can retrieve her and leave quickly, and suggests Dana's boost and songs, or another spell, once they know what ability the door uses. He has Gerk keep a hand on a shut door to test whether it can be kept and reused. When it vanishes as Gerk lets go, he concludes Gerk can open it again as long as Gerk is operating it. He calls keeping hostile things out the work of door guardians, says they have not chosen that name yet, stops the tests, and rides home. His lantern is pulled through the doors, dinged but intact, and he recovers it.
personality: Cautious about untested doorway effects. He checks a destination on foot before stepping through, treats the work as something that may improve with use, and stops once the far side turns hostile.
quotesThemes: It can work on a person and it can work on a place.
You might need to know the location. You can't just name a person, at least so far.
Maybe it'll just be you getting more used to it over time. Or perhaps there's something we need to unlock within you.
Their job, whatever they later call themselves, is not to let evil things through the doors.

Keystones.existing: Magical stones used to open and connect Atlas's Arch realms.
notes: Former gatekeepers treated them as something to receive and hide. That was a protection job, not a doorman's work. Carlkin finds it strange that they are being distributed again after they were collected.
Gatekeeper use works only in certain situations and is one-way. The keystone becomes part of the gate it opens and cannot be taken through that gate.

Plymouth said that with time and practice the keepers could use the keystones themselves. Sylan remembers Carlkin saying the party would not be able to open doors, and he is putting off that practice, including in his own realm.

Lich.existing: An unidentified lich whose phylactery may be hidden among mundane possessions.
notes: The party tells Carlkin that the phylactery is a mundane item the lich kept on his person and that the lich speaks to them telepathically. Carlkin calls that very worrisome and says to deal with it immediately.

Navi.existing: Ancient people tied to the Eldarin Tree, the keystones, and the Mother's Prayer.
notes: Carlkin says they have extra ways to move through Atlas, including teleportation magic carried in their own gear or people, and a strange little rod that teleports the user directionally across Atlas.

Abyssal eye-beast.existing: A god-tier extraplanar beast of oily tentacles and a wall of eyes.
notes: Carlkin describes the lighthouse incident as the party already nearly bringing an abyssal leviathan into his shop.

Doorway.existing: Gerk's Doorman passage: a supernatural door opened from nothing, distinct from a keystone gate.
notes: Distinct from a gatekeeper's keystone gate, and from plane shift, dimension door, teleport, and teleportation circles. It needs no keystone. Only Gerk can open this kind of portal, and only he can shut it. It can be opened and closed from either side, including after he has gone through.

If it is never shut, it remains a gateway until the space-time continuum collapses. Carlkin forbids practice underwater, in the lighthouse, or in his house, and wants it done in the woods or a large field. The party also avoids crowds and opening onto people. An earlier opening into the kitchen could have cut Mahali; that one was a critical success. A prior use involving the boat was described as ripping something out of reality.

Practice rules: picture a very specific target, do not think of nothing, never open underwater, always close it, and do not open it while moving. From the destination it is a stationary, featureless, door-shaped hole, compared to a green screen. Sound carries. A perfect opening has no flash, only ambient sound from the origin. While it is open, Gerk can feel the near door and the presence of the far end.

A Guidance 16 aimed about twenty feet outside the tavern door opens about a quarter mile southwest, near the road to New Navel, with the tavern and most of the stronghold visible. A natural 20 on Sylan, known to be in this realm at a known general location, with an intended offset of about ten feet, opens exactly ten feet behind him.

A total of 4 while thinking of Ciri, hidden in the forest but not at a known spot, opens onto an unrelated violent trench battlefield. Shutting it restores the forest except for a brimstone-sulfur smell and a black smudge on the grass.

A Guidance 19 toward a remembered Bouncing Betty upstairs hallway lands about twenty feet off, in the barn loft. Confusion is cited as snapping the exit to the stronger memory. The door then clicks and disappears when shut.

Opening furiously while raging, Guidance 17, focused on a lantern he is not looking at, produces a door about eighteen feet tall by seven feet wide and exits about a quarter mile south in the same forest. A bird disturbance marks that far end. Matter in the frame, such as canopy branches, becomes semi-translucent and is not destroyed while the door is open. Closing it severs those branches cleanly, with no burn and no debris. Sylan and Ciri can walk to that far end and return through it.

A normal, non-rage opening on a 9, aimed at a visible point about twenty-five feet away, still produces an eighteen-foot door and lands short, over the lantern. Two doors left open at once pull a vacuum strong enough to suck the lantern from one into the other. Shutting them stops the wind.

Size follows how it is opened. Force makes it larger. A gentle, low attempt produces an opening about six to eight inches by twelve inches, roughly a foot off the ground, and still misses: meant for open ground about a hundred feet from the house, it opens in the tomato field. The ability is usable three times a day, and recent destinations come up as favorites, which may make a recent place easier.

While Gerk keeps a hand on a shut door, it stays and acts like a normal door. It does not show the other side. Impacts from the far side are felt through it, and a strong enough hit could push him or fling it open. If his hand is knocked off, it opens to however far it was when he stopped touching it. When he deliberately lets go, the outline dissipates and the passage is gone. He can open these portals seemingly at will, with those caveats, as long as he is the one operating them.
openQuestions: What ability or magic the doorway uses.
How close Gerk can open a door, and what its exact range is.
What caused the racket and the bird disturbance at the far door, after no crater or other damage was found.

Langdale Stronghold.existing: The party's central stronghold and home base.
notes: Sylan suggests it as a private place for Gerk to practice. Carlkin says the party is much farther than five hundred feet from the castle, so reaching it is a walk.
The morning after the pub, the stronghold is shaking and smells of freshly baked buns. Breakfast is in the great hall. The lake has no island in the middle.
Guards are told that Sylan, Gerk, Ord, and Ciri went south into the forest, that Walker may arrive by dragon and may contact them, and that Mahali should have food ready for Glimmen.
Most of the stronghold is visible from the doorway that opened about a quarter mile southwest of the tavern. Gerk and Sylan return on mounts around midday rather than opening a door home.
While Walker waits in the Dragon Rider ruins, Plymouth is doing scribe work and taking etchings.

On an earlier Twin Peaks stop, the party picked him up for the Yowan and hid the last keystone from him until they arrived. Sylan remembers deliberately concealing it. The same stop is tied to a dragon and the last keystone.
He told the party that with time and practice they would be able to use the keystones themselves.
Walker asked Glimmen whether Vecna was still in the cave before they went back down. Walker is expected to arrive at the stronghold on Glimmen, and Mahali is asked to have food ready for the dragon.
Sylan asked Carlkin to examine a helm once the party's comrade returns. Carlkin agreed to schedule that by appointment.

He is shadowing Walker in the cave room and confirms it. He names the grassy atoll, Mount Elcastar, and Monkey Falls with its old obsidian ley-line marker, and teaches Walker the Weave and ley lines. He says Walker's training is lacking and must speed up or Walker will never beat Grixto.

He has visited only a few ley-line convergences and plans to go to this one soon if their other business stalls. The marker called Viablis has stood since he was a boy. He reads the clockwise rotation as Grixto moving the old intersection to a convergence Grixto has found.
He does not know the exact lich ritual. He treats the troop markers as toy soldiers, reads the eagle as a hobgoblin legion standard, and cannot explain the figurines without a map.

When stuck, he meditates. He sits mid-cave with Walker for several hours, coaching nasal, diaphragm breathing described as a wave, feeling the floor, and concentrating on where Walker needs to be, where he has to go, and what he needs to get there, so Walker can unweave rituals Grixto set for him.

He is the one Walker has been trying to listen to. He sets the eagle on the square table, says the repeated action now makes sense, and says the eagle has nothing to do with a mountain or a waterfall. He then asks for the cavalry markers rather than the rams. The explanation is cut off.

He assembled the square table, recognized the hunched eagle and troop tokens as a landmark map of how Grixto planned, and concludes they are in over their heads. He confirms the fifteen-degree obelisk offset means a conveyance, and that wards are amplified only nearby.

He once carried energy gems like Walker's and gave them to other prospective riders long ago. He can describe primal stones and offers to try condensing Walker's energy into them, with the risk that Walker loses part of himself into the stone. He wants more meditation before Walker channels.
personality: Blunt, didactic, and urgent about the gaps in Walker's training. He addresses Walker as 'my boy,' turns to meditation when a problem will not yield, and moves from brief excitement to alarm when the token pattern clicks.
quotesThemes: Your training is lacking. You must accelerate this or you'll never be able to beat Grixto.
The Weave is the magical network around us; ley lines are concentrations of it.
Magic on a ley line is like stepping into a fire pit while already on fire.
Unraveling the mysteries of the universe and playing toy soldiers.
Unravel the puzzle in front of you: where you need to be, where you have to go, and what you need to get there.
We were right. The obelisk is fifteen degrees where it should be here, meaning that there is a conveyance at that location.
Untrained channeling could inadvertently channel yourself into non-existence.

Ley line.existing: Lines of magic that gatehouses sit on.
notes: Elrus describes a ley line as a magical boundary that crisscrosses, a concentration of the Weave formed over eons. Some say Atlas's rotation created them; others compare them to magical latitude and longitude. Walker had not been taught this.
An old obsidian marker at Monkey Falls marks an intersection that would have been a highly magical site. Markers shift over millennia and have been moved or hidden because mages fought over them.

Spells cast on a line are bolstered, including teleportation for less energy. They are not a tunnel network between planes. The casting point must be within feet of a convergence. A convergence is rare. Grixto's rotated carvings point at one that moved, and Elrus considers it worth visiting.

The magical network around everything. Using energy produces a brief flash in which the surrounding magic can be seen. Ley lines are dense concentrations of it. Elrus treats it as basic knowledge Walker should already have.
One of the cave etchings: a flat island of rolling green plains, about the same size as the island used for comparison. Some maps label it the grassy atoll. Elrus says it has no real name.
The mountain among the four carved landmarks, named by Elrus from his notes.
The waterfall in the cave etchings. An old obsidian ley-line marker stands there, at what would have been an intersection and a highly magical site.

Scattered on the cave floor, in black stone and ivory, or possibly dark metal or bronze. Shapes include knight-like cavalry pieces, small etched dragons, pawn-like pieces marked for rank or unit size, and flat poker-chip tokens in two matched varieties with roughly equal counts.

One marker was removed from the table in the vision tied to the Raskina and is not in the room. Vecna's hunched eagle is a separate high-ranking piece, not one of the poker chips. Elrus treats the set as toy soldiers and sees no use for them without a map until the table reads them as a landmark map.
openQuestions: What the eagle and the cavalry markers mean on the table. Elrus turns to the cavalry pieces, not the rams, and the explanation is cut off.

notes: The high-ranking piece Vecna was tapping: a hunched eagle on a decorative base, not one of the poker-chip tokens. He left it on the table. Walker was still holding it, pocketed it, and later set it on Elrus's square table.

Elrus calls it a hobgoblin legion standard and says it has nothing to do with a mountain or a waterfall. Walker guesses it might be a tuning fork. In a recalled scene, Grixto pulls a different hunched eagle from a table and leaves once the plan is sorted.

Grixto.existing: Mobile antagonist tied to the Raskina and the earlier vision in this room.
notes: Elrus says Walker will never beat him unless training on ley lines and the Weave catches up. In the vision at this table, the figure who took a troop marker is the one the party linked to the Raskina.

He was a hobgoblin, and his legions would use an eagle as a standard. The hunched-eagle marker is read as a mark of a legion. A recalled scene shows him pull a different hunched eagle from a table and leave once the plan was sorted.
He carved the four landmarks rotated clockwise. Elrus reads that as Grixto locating a ley-line convergence that had moved. A spell for the working must be cast within feet of it.
The Al Kurin is already taken to have aided his lichdom. With the convergence and the Raskina, Elrus calls the set a deadly combination. He also left rituals for Walker to unweave.

Al Kurin.existing: Vessels containing the souls of dragons.
notes: Elrus says they already deduced Grixto had the Al Kurin to aid his lichdom, and that it is deadly combined with a ley-line convergence and the Raskina.

Raskina.existing: Vecna's red-skinned tome, made from his sister and held by Grixto.
notes: The party identified it in the vision. Walker calls it the sister-skin book, and the DM accepts that as colloquial wording he did not expect. Elrus includes it with the Al Kurin and the ley-line convergence in the working he expects was used for Grixto's lichdom.
quotesThemes: Sister-skin book

Phylactery.existing: A vessel containing a lich's soul.
notes: Elrus says phylacteries are usually gems of some kind. Becoming a lich is an ancient ritual whose exact method he does not know, not simply declaring an ordinary object the vessel. Any magical requirement would be strengthened at a ley-line convergence.
What the party told Carlkin is different: that this lich's phylactery is a mundane item he kept on his person.
openQuestions: What the ancient lich ritual requires, and whether this phylactery is a mundane object or a gem.

notes: A landmark that has stood since Elrus was a boy. It is only rumored to be a ley line, and Elrus is concerned that Grixto carved it into the wall.
Elrus's explanation for why a few hours in the cave feel like weeks to Walker. Separately, Walker's time on the Reach runs about seven of his days for each day the party experiences.

Ciri.existing: Half-elf rogue, keeper of Lith's keystone.
notes: Already at the New Navel pub when the others arrive, drunk enough that she can no longer stealth: crouched in the corner behind a pile of mugs, convinced she is hidden. At breakfast her face is in the buns.

She has a room in the tavern, spends the night there, and rejoins the others on the path up to the stronghold in the same clothes, carrying her boots. She goes south into the forest with Sylan, Gerk, and Ord.

She lies down trying to nap, then hides in the forest so Gerk can open a door to her without seeing where she goes. Her stealth roll is 7 on the die. One report gives 23 as the total and another says the 7 did not beat a 23.

After the door misses her, she throws her voice to answer, then stays in a tree and watches. She later goes with Sylan to inspect the far end and returns through the portal, noticed as a shadow passing behind him.

New Navel.existing: A familiar stop that sends trade caravans to the party's tavern in Langdale and holds Carlkin's lighthouse.
notes: Midday on the party's sixth day. People are out on ordinary business, and traders are coming through for trade associated with New Navel. The group with Sylan is outside Carlkin's lighthouse, then Ord, Sylan, and Gerk go to the pub. A day and a half remains on the current clock.
The road between the tavern and New Navel passes near the mis-aimed doorway, about a quarter mile southwest of the tavern. Three human traders with a mule cart were traveling that road.

With Gerk and Sylan at Carlkin's, then at the pub. At breakfast in the great hall he is eating a hot bun. Gerk looks to him before accepting Sylan as trainer and asks if he will come along. He comes south into the forest to watch the doorway practice.

Mahali.existing: Elder god and the party's chef at the stronghold.
notes: Asked, via the guards, to prepare food for Glimmen ahead of Walker's expected arrival by dragon. Sylan says an earlier doorway into the kitchen could have cut Mahali. The DM says that opening was a critical success. Mahali is not present for the forest practice.

Sylan chooses it for Gerk's doorway practice and explicitly avoids the nearby bees. The practice is also described as starting from the Langdale forest outskirts, out of view of the red-flag runes.

Raven Queen.existing: Elder god of death, also called Nira.

Twin Peaks.existing: Mountain range on the route between the wider world and Langdale.
notes: Gerk has been there often and has friends and fond memories there. He remembers it better than the frozen gatehouse at Volga. The tavern they mean sits on a busy street if entered by the front door.
Sylan suggests a short visit, possibly to say hello or have lunch, once this training is done. They had told people they would be in the forest.

Bouncing Betty.existing: Inn and tavern in Twin Peaks. Also heard as Bouncing Benny's.
notes: The Twin Peaks tavern Gerk wants as the doorway target. He aims for the upstairs hallway in front of the rooms because the front door opens onto a busy street. The party argues the name and whether this building or another local tavern has the large stage they remember.

The upstairs is the sleeping area in the DM's usual tavern layout. One account gives the inn a third floor, and Sylan says the rooms have been moved since they were last familiar with the layout. The party has slept there in game, but not recently. The last stop was before the long boat trip toward Lake Nyx, around the time they collected Plymouth.

Its barn was rebuilt. From the barn's second story you look down on stables and a wagon set in the center. Gerk has slept in the barn more than once. An old sideline ended there: a wayward bard and a drunk wizard killed a mule or donkey with a levitation spell and left the body, and the party made some gold. Confusion shifts Gerk's doorway from the upstairs hall to that loft, about twenty feet off.
openQuestions: Whether the stage they remember belongs to Bouncing Betty or to a different tavern.

Confusion Effect.existing: A spell effect that leaves its victim confused and unable to act meaningfully.
notes: While Gerk is opening a doorway, confusion shifts the destination from the pictured upstairs hallway to a more familiar memory, the loft of Bouncing Betty's barn, about twenty feet off.

Nyx.existing: Nyx may hold hobgoblins who know where the lich is hiding.
notes: Reached via Lake Nyx by boat. The DM describes that voyage as about one to two months. The Bouncing Betty visit was before the party went over to Lake Nyx, and they were still in Nyx's area afterward.
Sylan says that when Nawaka returned he could always send them, and that Nawaka has the ability to message them and did not forget or choose not to. The party had said they would be in the forest.

It was sitting near the point Gerk tried to open onto, past a crossing. The vacuum between two open doors sucked it through. It rolled and was left dinged, but it was not shattered. Sylan recovered it.

Sylan's sister.existing: Sylan's sister, whom he hopes to bring home.
notes: Sylan suggests using Gerk's doorway to reach her and get back out quickly. They do not try it. Gerk will not doorway to her after the failed attempt to reach Ciri without knowing where she was.

Dana.existing: Half-elf cleric and Gatekeeper of the Pitel keystone.
notes: Sylan says she can boost other people and that her songs work well, and he hopes that could help Gerk's doorway. She is not present for the test.
