newTerms.name: Earth, wind, sea, and fire sigil
notes: Sigil Walker uncovered at the end of the previous session, before the table returned to Carlkin, tied to his deciphering of the shifted landmarks.

newTerms.name: Navi directional rod
notes: Small rod Carlkin attributes to the Navi. It teleports the user directionally across Atlas, separate from keystones and from Gerk's doors.

newTerms.name: Radially shifted landmarks
notes: Obelisk, island, waterfall, and mountain peak, each offset from its true place when judged from the old dragon rider guild tower.

newTerms.name: Helm
notes: Unspecified helm Sylan wants Carlkin to examine by appointment once a comrade returns. Carlkin agrees to schedule it.

newTerms.name: Troop markers
notes: Figurines in the Dragon Rider cave, black stone and ivory or possibly dark metal or bronze: knights, etched dragons, and ranked pawns. Walker treats them as ordinary, unlike Vecna's special rocks.

On the activated table, cavalry and infantry pieces appear as small semi-animated holographic troop markings relative to the landmarks. Distinct from the flat landmark tokens and from the hunched eagle.

newTerms.name: Hunched eagle marker
notes: High-ranking hunched eagle on a decorative base, read as a hobgoblin legion standard. Vecna tapped one and left it on the stone table; Walker pocketed it. Grixto took a different one from a table once a plan was ready.
Set on Elrus's square table, it flashes the illusion battlefield. It is unrelated to the mountain or the waterfall. Walker first guessed it was a tuning fork.

newTerms.name: The Weave
notes: Magical network surrounding everything, briefly visible as a flash when energy is used. Ley lines are concentrations of it. Elrus expects Walker to know it; Walker does not.

newTerms.name: Grassy atoll
notes: Map label for an otherwise unnamed flat green island of rolling plains, about the size of the island they are on, among the four cave-etching landmarks.

newTerms.name: Mount Elcastar
notes: The mountain landmark in the cave etchings.

newTerms.name: Monkey Falls
notes: Waterfall landmark in the cave etchings, site of an old obsidian ley-line marker. Walker does not yet know what a ley line is.

newTerms.name: Ley line convergence
notes: A rare intersection where magic is greatly strengthened and a spell must be cast within feet of the point. Grixto's rotated carvings mark one that has moved.

newTerms.name: Viablis
notes: Long-standing landmark, present since Elrus was a boy, only rumored to be a ley line, and carved by Grixto.

newTerms.name: Time dilation
notes: Elrus's name for why a few hours in the cave feels much longer.

newTerms.name: Midgar week
notes: The unit Walker used for his check-in: one week of party time on Midgar, not one week of his own faster time. Seven of his days pass for each party day, so a Midgar week is about forty-nine days for him.

newTerms.name: Flavian
notes: Name given for a woman on staff, recalled as manager of the party's tavern. The DM was unsure.

newTerms.name: Dullhurst
notes: Place traders come from, or from beyond, to trade at New Navel. Spelling and identity are unconfirmed.

newTerms.name: Rita
notes: Heard beside New Navel as another place those traders are here to deal in. Spelling and identity are unconfirmed.

newTerms.name: Southern stream clearing
notes: Forest clearing south of the stronghold, by a stream, with remnants of buildings. Used for Gerk's doorway training. Bees are nearby and avoided.

newTerms.name: Red flag
notes: Marker a decent way into the southern Langdale forest, not at the edge. The DM says it marks runes found earlier in the hobgoblin search, heard as Paulette runes, near the stream clearing. The party did not go there for this practice.

newTerms.name: Halo Heart
notes: A place Sylan wants Gerk to picture while training the doorway, and not to open onto yet, instead of returning home before the mission is done.

newTerms.name: Trench battlefield glimpse
notes: Unnamed place behind the bad door: explosions and noise, a trench embankment, an orc and a human in mixed medieval and French Renaissance dress, metal tube weapons, a shouted unknown language, and a small clay pot. Closing the door left a sulfur smell and a black smudge.

newTerms.name: Volga
notes: Recent stop with a tall frozen gatehouse the party climbed. Cold, a little spooky, and tied to a spear-in-the-head memory. Gerk's recollection is weak.

newTerms.name: Twin Peaks
notes: Place Gerk knows well, with friends and fond memories. He used this name for the doorway-training destination; the group also called the tavern Bouncing Betty and could not agree they were separate. The party may stop in after training.

newTerms.name: Bouncing Betty
notes: Twin Peaks inn whose name is unsettled: also heard as Bouncing Benny, bouncing beddy, Bouncy and Betty's, and bouncing beddies. Gerk wants the upstairs room hallway; the front door faces a busy street. Floor count is disputed, and a remembered stage may belong to a different tavern.

Guest rooms are upstairs. A rebuilt barn has a second-story loft over stables and a wagon, where Gerk has slept. A past bard-and-wizard levitation show there killed a donkey or mule and paid the party. The doorway opened onto that loft.

newTerms.name: Nawaka
notes: Person Sylan says can message the party. They expected word from him after saying they would be in the forest.

newTerms.name: Yowan
notes: Destination where the party brought Plymouth and only then revealed they had the keystone. Heard as 'the Yowan.'

newTerms.name: Lake Nyx
notes: Where the party went after their earlier Bouncing Betty stop. The DM describes the boat trip there as on the order of one to two months.

newTerms.name: Sylan's lantern
notes: A lantern of Sylan's that was near Gerk's aim point. Two open doors sucked it through; it was dinged but not broken.

newTerms.name: Doorway shear
notes: Closing one of Gerk's doorways cuts cleanly through whatever lies in the plane, with no burn and no debris. Branches were severed when the doors shut. Two open doorways also pull a strong wind between them.

newTerms.name: Doorway favorites
notes: Gerk can open the door three times a day. Recent destinations seem to surface as favorites or ready options, and a place may be easier if he has been there recently.

newTerms.name: Kawaica
notes: Unsettled name for the person whose house and tomato field Gerk aimed at. Also heard as Growcause and Kroka. Sylan thinks the growling on the far side of the doggy door is that person's pet.

newTerms.name: Landmark tokens
notes: Flat poker-chip tokens, distinct from the troop figurines. Four, placed cardinally, become landmark representations and are already at their usable area. More tokens for known landmarks, or other pieces, would extend the map. How they are made is unknown.

newTerms.name: Illusion war table
notes: A square table Elrus put together that projects a battlefield or other scenario from the right tokens. Placing the hunched eagle with the landmark and troop pieces flashes a partial map. He treats it as the tool behind Grixto's military planning; Vecna and Grixto have used the same kind of piece.

newTerms.name: Conveyance
notes: Elrus's name for what an obelisk fifteen degrees off true indicates. Near it, Walker's wards and shields are amplified, then the boost wanes after he leaves. Channeling it without training could destroy the caster; with more power he might channel it deliberately.

newTerms.name: Primal stones
notes: Raw magic condensed into a stone. The creator stops being the sole director of that magic: a craftsperson can make items or call the energy, or the stone can be broken to release a torrent. Making one could leave part of the person in the stone. Walker must choose a primal source he is attuned to.
